correctness.rationale: The two-element Kneser representation gives an unambiguous ten-vertex host; both standard and strict move rules are enumerated exhaustively. Since every move consumes two and creates one pebble, reachability recursion strictly decreases total mass and exactly covers all legal finite sequences by first-step induction. Independent Python recursive and C++17 queue implementations agree across all 286 states of weights below four and all 715 weight-four states; they reproduce occupancy partitions, singleton support forest spectra, and the 17 S5 orbit check. Four-pebble optimality itself is an existing theorem; the new finite census is fully reproduced by the supplied code.

value.rationale: The natural question asks how many minimum resource placements work and which arrangements benefit from pooling at two distinct neighbors. Despite the already-known equal optimum counts four, unrestricted rubbling admits 175 workable arrangements, while ordinary pebbling admits only ten: the difference of 165 is a substantial operational distinction, not a small parameter increment. The structural classification of all optimum supports, including 90 entirely separated configurations and a sharp triangle criterion for the 2+1+1 case, is precise and reusable as a benchmark for optimal configuration robustness. The fact is finite but a complete classification of a canonical graph invariant rather than an arbitrary slice.
